title: Bench
subtitle: Software person to hardware interaction designer, one hour a day, 168 days.
rubric: can explain both why and how

Hshop.note: Maker favourite. Modules, sensors, dev boards. Ships nationwide in 1-3 days.

Nshop.where: 1 Bui Xuan Phai, Tay Thanh, Tan Phu, HCMC
Nshop.note: Same category as Hshop. Cross-check stock and price between the two.

TheGioiIC.note: Serious component distributor. Go here for discretes, passives, connectors, ICs by part number.

ICDayRoi.note: Good for odd single components and ICs.

NhatTao.note: The physical market. Go in person for tools, wire, connectors, salvage, and to handle parts before buying. Haggle.

Shopee.note: Cheapest for generic tools, craft supplies, consumables. Check seller rating; 2-5 days.

JLCPCB.note: PCB fab. 5 boards from about 2 USD plus shipping. DHL to VN is roughly 5-10 days.

SQFMI.note: Watchy itself. Longest lead time of anything on this list. Order it early or plan a substitute.

AliExpress.note: For parts no HCMC shop stocks. Cheap, but two to five weeks to Vietnam. Order in week 1 or not at all.

craft.name: Craft kit: tam formex (PVC foam board) 3-5mm, corrugated card, craft knife, cutting mat, masking tape, glue stick, sticky notes
craft.why: Phase 01 runs entirely on cardboard. Crude and fast beats neat and slow.

notebook.name: A5 plain notebook and a fine black pen
notebook.why: Every interaction study is drawn before it is built. Paper, not Figma.

esp32s3.name: ESP32-S3 dev board (DevKitC-1 or equivalent) x2
esp32s3.why: The MCU for the whole course. Two, because you will brick one and because comparing is how you debug.
esp32s3.vnd: 230k dev kit, or 135k bare WROOM-1 module

breadboard.name: Breadboard 830-point x2, jumper wire set (M-M, M-F, F-F), 22AWG solid hookup wire
breadboard.why: Ugly wires are welcome guests. Two boards so a working circuit can survive while you build the next.

passives.name: Resistor assortment kit, ceramic and electrolytic cap assortment, LED assortment (3mm/5mm)
passives.why: You will reach for a 10k pull-up at 22:00 and no shop is open.

inputs.name: Tactile buttons (assorted heights), EC11 rotary encoder x2, 10k potentiometer x2, slide and toggle switches
inputs.why: Phase 01 taught you that feel is the design. These are the parts where feel lives.

multimeter.name: Digital multimeter with continuity beep
multimeter.why: Non-negotiable. Continuity and voltage are how you stop guessing.

soldering.name: Temperature-controlled soldering iron, leaded solder 0.6mm, flux pen, desoldering wick, stand, brass sponge
soldering.why: Breadboards lie about connections. From week 7 you need joints that hold.

handtools.name: Flush cutters, wire strippers, fine tweezers, helping-hands or small vice, hex/screwdriver set
handtools.why: The tools you resent buying until the first time you have them.

oled.name: SSD1306 0.96 inch OLED, I2C
oled.why: Your first bus device. Small enough that you must decide what not to show.

imu.name: IMU: MPU6050 or LSM6DS3
imu.why: Motion as an input. Wrist gestures, orientation, tap detect.

haptic_basic.name: Coin vibration motor (ERM) x3, NPN transistor (2N2222/S8050), flyback diodes
haptic_basic.why: An MCU pin cannot drive a motor. Learning why is the point.

power.name: LiPo 3.7V 500-1000mAh with JST-PH, TP4056 charging module x2, USB-C cables, 2-pin JST pigtails
power.why: A device that has to be plugged in is a desk ornament. Battery changes every decision.

watchy.name: Watchy v3 (SQFMI)
watchy.why: Your dissection specimen: open hardware, open firmware, real power-management behaviour. Ships E-express to Vietnam in 7-14 business days, so it is not the long pole -- the DRV2605L is. Order it in week 1 anyway; it is the one part week 8 is built around.
watchy.vnd: board price at checkout, plus 5.99 USD shipping
watchy.note_verified: Shipping verified at SQFMI checkout 2026-08-13: E-express, 7-14 business days, 5.99 USD to Vietnam.

haptic_lra.name: DRV2605L haptic driver breakout + LRA motor
haptic_lra.why: ERM buzzes. LRA speaks. You cannot design a haptic language on a pager motor. Neither Hshop nor Nshop carries this, so it is an import: order it in week 1 or week 9 runs on ERM with a narrower vocabulary.

audio.name: MAX98357A I2S amp + small 4-ohm speaker, plus INMP441 or SPH0645 I2S microphone
audio.why: Sound and haptics are one system. You need to make both, and hear a room.

sense.name: APDS-9960 gesture/proximity/light sensor, VL53L0X time-of-flight sensor
sense.why: Presence and approach: the inputs that let a device act before it is touched.

leds.name: WS2812B / SK6812 LED ring (12 or 16) and a short strip
leds.why: Addressable light is a full expressive channel, not an indicator.

caliper.name: Digital caliper, 0.01mm, 150mm
caliper.why: CAD starts with measuring something real. Guessed dimensions print as garbage.

printing.name: 3D printing budget: a local FDM/SLA service, or your own printer
printing.why: Phase 04 is print-touch-revise. Budget for roughly 10-15 small parts across four weeks.
printing.vnd: 600k-1.5M for the phase via a service

finishing.name: Sandpaper 200-1000 grit, needle files, superglue, 5-min epoxy, M2/M3 screw assortment, M2/M3 heat-set inserts
finishing.why: The difference between a print and an object is forty minutes of finishing.

smd.name: 0603/0805 resistor and capacitor books, USB-C receptacle x5, 3.3V LDO x5, ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 module x3
smd.why: The parts that go on your own board. Buy spares of everything; you will lose one to the floor.

rework.name: Solder paste (Sn63Pb37 in a syringe), hot air rework station or a cheap hot plate, isopropyl alcohol, flux
rework.why: Hand-soldering a WROOM module is possible and miserable. Reflow once and you will not go back.

fab.name: PCB fabrication order: 5 boards, 2-layer, plus a stencil if you are reflowing
fab.why: The moment the spaghetti becomes a product.

phases.title: Interaction as a material
phases.question: How should a physical product behave?
phases.milestone: A Wizard-of-Oz device a stranger used, on video, plus the interaction studies behind it
phases.brief: Before a single wire. Learn to ask whether a thing should be a button, a gesture, a light, a sound, a haptic, an automatic behaviour, or nothing at all. Everything this phase is cardboard, paper and your phone. Crude on purpose.

phases.title: Physical computing
phases.question: How do I make software touch the physical world?
phases.milestone: Watchy running firmware you wrote, plus your own breadboard device that sleeps, wakes and responds
phases.brief: Your software brain learns atoms. Skip the beginner programming entirely: go straight at voltage, GPIO, analog, PWM, I2C, SPI, interrupts, power and sleep. The parts arrive this phase, so they must be ordered in Phase 01.

phases.title: Multimodal and intelligent interaction
phases.question: What happens beyond screens?
phases.milestone: A physical AI prototype using at least three modalities, tested on a real person
phases.brief: You already know how to make something intelligent. This phase is about how intelligence should behave physically: haptic primitives, audio-haptic choreography, when to stay silent, and faking the model convincingly enough to find out if the behaviour is even wanted.

phases.title: Industrial design and CAD
phases.question: How does behaviour become an object?
phases.milestone: Three physical iterations of one enclosure, on a desk, in order, with the notes that drove each revision
phases.brief: CAD taught as construction, not as beautiful shapes. Sketch constraints, parametric dimensions, shells, components, joints, clearances. Then print, touch, find the problem, and go back. Renders are not the deliverable; objects are.

phases.title: Electronics and PCB
phases.question: How does a prototype become real hardware?
phases.milestone: A deliberately boring first PCB, reviewed against the silicon vendor's own checklist, ordered and paid for
phases.brief: Deliberately late. By now you have met the physical reason for every component you are placing. Schematic, footprints, layout, DRC, gerbers, then power and Li-ion charging. Use a module for the radio; do not design an antenna in your first month.

phases.title: Integrated product
phases.question: Can I make something portfolio-worthy?
phases.milestone: One finished physical-digital product, in five people's hands, documented well enough to explain both why and how
phases.brief: No new subject. The disciplines collapse together: form, interaction, electronics, software, intelligence. Return to the prototype loop and keep iterating with actual people until it holds together.

weeks.title: Input, behaviour, feedback
weeks.arc: Learn to see any object as a set of input-to-behaviour-to-feedback triples, and to notice which ones were chosen rather than inherited.
covers: the rubric you are training against

project.name: The Interaction Autopsy
project.spec: Pick three physical objects you own that could not be more different: something with a screen, something with none, something with exactly one control. Map every interaction each one supports as input to behaviour to feedback. Mark each triple as chosen or inherited.
project.deliverable: Three hand-drawn A5 cards, photographed, one object per card
project.stretch: Find one triple in each object you believe is wrong, and say what it should have been

sources: Apple Watch Design Tips and Tricks (WWDC15)

weeks.title: Choosing the modality
weeks.arc: Button, gesture, sound, light, haptic, automatic, or nothing. The choice is the design work; everything after is execution.

project.name: The Modality Swap
project.spec: Take one interaction from your autopsy and redesign it five ways: as a physical control, as a gesture, as sound, as light, and as an automatic behaviour with no input at all. Build a crude prototype of each.
project.deliverable: Five prototypes on one table, photographed, plus a written verdict naming the right one and why the other four lose
project.stretch: Make someone else pick before you tell them your answer

sources: Nothing design team on returning to physical controls

weeks.title: State, time and feedback
weeks.arc: How a product tells you what it is doing, what it just did, and what it is about to do, without a paragraph of text.

project.name: The Status Object
project.spec: Build a non-screen object that communicates one continuously changing state. Cardboard, paper dials, a phone used only as a light source. No words allowed anywhere on it.
project.deliverable: An object a stranger can read correctly within ten seconds with no instruction, proven on one actual stranger
project.stretch: Make it legible from across a room and from arm's length, differently

weeks.title: Crude prototypes and the Wizard
weeks.arc: Make it tangible enough to learn something, put it in a hand, watch what actually happens. Fidelity is a cost, not a virtue.
covers: what to prototype and what to fake

project.name: The Puppet
project.spec: A cardboard device that you secretly operate while another person uses it. They believe it is autonomous. You are the intelligence behind the curtain.
project.deliverable: Video of one real person using it without knowing, plus the list of behaviours you found yourself improvising
project.stretch: Run it twice with two people and change one rule between runs

sources: IDEO Design Kit determine what to prototype
Google UX Engineering on simulating intelligence

weeks.title: Current you can reason about
weeks.arc: Voltage, current, resistance, GPIO, digital in and out. Enough electricity to stop being superstitious about it.

project.name: First Light
project.spec: Blink, then a button, then a debounced button, then a PWM fade, then all four combined on one ESP32-S3. Draw the circuit by hand before you build it.
project.deliverable: Working circuit on video, plus your hand-drawn schematic photographed next to it
project.stretch: Measure the actual current through your LED and explain the difference from the value you calculated

weeks.title: Analog, timing and feel
weeks.arc: The physical world is continuous and noisy. Sampling, smoothing and response curves are where feel is actually made.

project.name: The Feel Rig
project.spec: A knob driving a light and a vibration motor, with three switchable response curves: linear, exponential, and one you tune by hand until it feels right.
project.deliverable: The rig, plus a written verdict on which curve feels right and a guess at why
project.stretch: Get two other people to rank the curves blind and see if they agree with you

sources: Arduino official learn: PWM and analog

weeks.title: Buses, parts and a panel
weeks.arc: I2C and SPI, and the fact that a component is a datasheet plus a protocol, not a mystery.

project.name: The Panel
project.spec: OLED over I2C, an IMU, an encoder and a haptic motor on one breadboard, working together as one small coherent interface rather than four demos.
project.deliverable: A panel that does one thing well, on video, with the encoder-to-screen-to-haptic loop feeling like a single object
project.stretch: Solder the messiest sub-circuit onto perfboard so it survives being carried

sources: Arduino official learn: I2C and SPI

weeks.title: Watchy, power, sleep and wake
weeks.arc: Consumer hardware is defined by what it does while apparently doing nothing. Deep sleep is a design constraint, not an optimisation.
covers: reading open hardware as a document

project.name: The Watch That Is Not a Watch
project.spec: Reflash Watchy so it does something that is not telling the time, using its real wake-and-sleep cycle. Then build your own module device that sleeps, wakes on an input, acts, and sleeps again.
project.deliverable: Watchy running your firmware, plus your own device measured drawing real sleep current
project.stretch: Get your own device under 1mA asleep and say what is still eating the difference

weeks.title: Haptics as a language
weeks.arc: Haptic primitives, rhythm and texture. A vocabulary someone can learn without being taught.

project.name: The Haptic Alphabet
project.spec: Design six haptic patterns intended to mean six different things. Then test whether a person, holding the device out of sight, can tell them apart.
project.deliverable: The six patterns plus a confusion matrix from one real test subject
project.stretch: Redesign the two that got confused most and retest

sources: Google Sound and Touch: design beyond the screen

weeks.title: Sound and choreography
weeks.arc: Light, sound and haptic arriving as one event rather than three. Synchronisation is the whole trick.
covers: when sound is the wrong channel

project.name: The Chord
project.spec: One single event, expressed as light plus sound plus haptic together. Build three versions with different timing relationships and tune until one of them stops feeling like three things.
project.deliverable: Three versions, A/B tested on a real person, and their answer recorded before you give yours
project.stretch: Make a version that works with the sound muted and loses nothing important

weeks.title: Ambient, calm and the interruption budget
weeks.arc: When should a computer disappear into the environment instead of demanding attention? Every notification is a withdrawal from a finite account.

project.name: The Thing That Shuts Up
project.spec: A device that holds information but says almost nothing. It must sense presence or approach, and it must have explicit written rules for when it is allowed to speak.
project.deliverable: Working prototype plus your interruption budget written as rules a stranger could apply
project.stretch: Live with it for three days and count every time it was wrong

weeks.title: Simulating intelligence
weeks.arc: Fake the model convincingly enough to find out whether the behaviour is wanted at all, before you build any of it.
covers: Wizard of Oz on real hardware
confidence and hedging in physical feedback
lessons from shipping an ML consumer object

project.name: The Wizard
project.spec: Take your Phase 03 hardware and drive its intelligent behaviour yourself, live, from a laptop, while a real person uses it believing it is autonomous. At least three modalities must be involved.
project.deliverable: Video of a real user, plus a written spec of what the model would actually need to do, including how it should behave when unsure
project.stretch: Run it once where you deliberately get it wrong, and design the recovery

weeks.title: Parametric thinking
weeks.arc: CAD as construction. Sketches, constraints and dimensions that hold a design together when you change your mind.

project.name: The Measured Copy
project.spec: Caliper an object you own that has at least one curve and one hole. Rebuild it in Fusion from your measurements alone, then print or mock it and compare.
project.deliverable: The CAD file plus a dimensional error report: where you were wrong and by how much
project.stretch: Make one parameter drive three features, then change it and watch nothing break

weeks.title: Enclosure construction
weeks.arc: Shells, bosses, ribs, components and joints. How a plastic thing is actually put together.

project.name: The Two-Part Box
project.spec: A shelled two-part enclosure with a lid, boss posts for M2 screws, a hole a real button passes through, and a slot for a real cable.
project.deliverable: CAD plus the first physical print, with the electronics from Phase 02 actually inside it
project.stretch: Add heat-set inserts and have the lid close on screws that do not strip

weeks.title: Fit, tolerance and the snap
weeks.arc: Nothing fits on the first print. Learn your own process's real clearance instead of trusting a number from a blog.

project.name: The Fit Ladder
project.spec: Print a tolerance ladder that steps clearance from 0.1mm to 0.6mm, find the value that actually works for your printer or print service, then design a snap-fit lid using it.
project.deliverable: The ladder with the working step marked, plus a lid that snaps, holds, and opens again without breaking
project.stretch: Make the snap audible and tune the click

weeks.title: Product anatomy
weeks.arc: Open real products. Battery placement, flex cables, antennas, seals, stacked boards, speakers, motors. Packaging is a design discipline.

project.name: The Enclosure, Mk I to III
project.spec: Three physical iterations of a real enclosure for your Phase 03 prototype, each driven by a specific problem you found by holding the previous one.
project.deliverable: Three prints on a desk in order, photographed, each with the one-line reason it was replaced
project.stretch: Have someone else hold Mk I and Mk III and say what changed without being told

weeks.title: Schematic literacy
weeks.arc: A schematic is a document you read, not art you produce. Learn to read one before drawing your own.

project.name: The Redraw
project.spec: Redraw one section of the Watchy schematic in KiCad from scratch without copying, then diff yours against the original.
project.deliverable: Your schematic plus a written list of everything you got wrong or omitted
project.stretch: Explain the purpose of every capacitor you left out

weeks.title: Footprints and layout
weeks.arc: Symbols connect to footprints, footprints become copper, copper has physics. DRC is the first honest reviewer you will meet.

project.name: The Breakout
project.spec: Lay out a trivial two-layer board: an ESP32-S3 module footprint, USB-C, two buttons, one LED, and a header. It does not need to be clever. It needs to pass DRC.
project.deliverable: Clean DRC, exported gerbers, and a 3D render of the board
project.stretch: Route it twice, once badly on purpose, and say what makes the good one good

weeks.title: Vendor constraints and review
weeks.arc: Switch from maker tutorials to silicon-vendor documentation. RF and layout constraints get real very quickly.

project.name: The Review
project.spec: Take your board through Espressif's own schematic and layout checklists line by line, then run a self-review as if you were signing off someone else's work.
project.deliverable: The annotated checklist with every item answered, plus a rev B that fixes what it found
project.stretch: Have one other engineer review it and count what you both missed

weeks.title: Power, battery and fab
weeks.arc: Li-ion charging and power path from the semiconductor vendor, not from a blog diagram. Then you press order.

project.name: The Boring Board
project.spec: Add Li-ion charging and power path to your board, finish DRC, generate the fabrication package, and actually order five boards from JLCPCB.
project.deliverable: Order confirmation, the BOM, and a one-paragraph note on what you expect to have got wrong
project.stretch: Order a stencil and plan the reflow

weeks.title: Concept lock
weeks.arc: Stop exploring. Name the product, the person, and the one interaction that justifies its existence.
covers: scoping to what can ship in four weeks

project.name: The One Sentence
project.spec: Lock the final product. One sentence of intent, one named user, one interaction that could not exist as an app. Then build a non-working physical mock of it at final size.
project.deliverable: A one-page spec plus a full-size mock you can carry in a pocket or set on a desk
project.stretch: Show the mock to someone and have them tell you what it does

sources: Nothing Hardware Interaction Designer role, third reading

weeks.title: Bring-up and integration
weeks.arc: Assemble, flash, and get every subsystem alive one at a time. Bring-up is a discipline with an order.
covers: debugging a board rather than a breadboard

project.name: Bring-Up
project.spec: Assemble your board, power it safely, and bring up each subsystem in order: power, USB, MCU, then each peripheral. Get it into the enclosure.
project.deliverable: Working hardware inside your Mk III enclosure, running your firmware, on video
project.stretch: Write the bring-up log as a document someone else could follow

weeks.title: Five hands
weeks.arc: Put it in real hands and watch. Not a demo, not a pitch. Watch, shut up, and take notes.
covers: deciding what feedback to act on

project.name: Five Hands
project.spec: Five people, no explanation, ten seconds of silence each before you say anything. Then two revisions driven by what you saw, not by what they said.
project.deliverable: Five sets of notes and two shipped revisions, with the reason for each change
project.stretch: Find the one thing all five did that you did not design for

weeks.title: The telling
weeks.arc: A portfolio piece is not the object. It is the object plus the argument for it, in a form someone can absorb in ninety seconds.
covers: writing the why and the how
the Nothing rubric as a final check

project.name: The Piece
project.spec: Photograph it, film the interaction, and write it up so it answers both why and how. Then score yourself against all eight lines of the Nothing rubric.
project.deliverable: A published portfolio piece plus your honest rubric score with evidence for each line
project.stretch: Send it to one person in the industry who owes you nothing

sources: Nothing Hardware Interaction Designer role, final reading

objects.rule: One real product or teardown per card, with one sentence on why its interaction is the way it is. Never repeat an object -- `bench.py ledger` lists every one already used. The object is not homework; it is the thing that makes the card worth opening.

veins: Something in his own house he has never opened. The best object is often on the desk.
Cho Nhat Tao: salvage, dead Vietnamese consumer electronics, things with worn buttons.
Vietnamese products specifically -- rice cookers, motorbike dashboards, karaoke remotes, ATM keypads. A curriculum built only on Californian objects teaches a narrow eye.
Objects that outlived their category: F-91W, Nokia 3310, Zippo, Bic Cristal, the 3.5mm jack.
A device someone else in the room uses differently than he does.
Deliberate failures: Juicero, Ouya, the Pixel 4 Soli gestures, touch-only headphone controls.
